Nas Jaafar won the 2026 World Brewers Cup in Brussels by centering his routine around the theme of "resistance". He used a Panama Geisha coffee to demonstrate how friction at origin, during grinding, and in brewing shapes the cup. His two-stage recipe balances percolation and immersion.

The Setup
- Coffee: 15g Panama Geisha (Finca Nuguo Anaerobic Natural)
- Grinder: Option-O Lagom 01 (set to ~700 microns)
- Brewer: UFO V3 with a Hario Switch Base
- Paper Filter: HiFlux
- Water: 200g total (92°C, 50 ppm, balanced Magnesium and Calcium)

The Routine and Recipe
1. 0:00 - The Percolation Stage: Pour 100g of water in circular motions to capture red florals and citric acidity. Allow it to percolate.
2. 0:58 - Close the Valve: Close the switch on the brewer base to create controlled outflow resistance and stop the water flow.
3. 1:00 - The Immersion Stage: Pour the final 100g of water, shifting to contact time-driven immersion to develop sugarcane sweetness and a smooth body.
4. 2:00 - Open the Valve: Open the switch again and let the coffee percolate for 10 seconds.
5. 2:10 - Finish: Close the switch to complete the brew

Aromatic Profile
- Aroma: Intense notes of hibiscus, mandarin orange, and sweet sugarcane.

Flavor and Acidity (by Temperature)
- Hot: Medium intensity, vibrant citric acidity. Forward notes of mandarin orange and a fruity sweetness.
- Warm: Shifting toward a lively malic acidity. Prominent notes of apricot and crisp red apple.
- Cold: Sweetness becomes more distinct, leaning into sugarcane and red apple flavors with a long, clean aftertaste.

Mouthfeel and Structure
- Body: Medium intensity, exceptionally smooth and clear.
- Finish: Highly balanced and structured, intentionally leaving a lingering sweetness rather than any bitter dryness.
